podcast.body: This song was the third in Willie Nelson's set list for the Austin City Limits pilot in 1974 and was crucial for his desired creative control. Originally written by Nelson for his 1970 album "Both Sides Now" (then titled "Bloody Merry"), it was heard by Atlantic Records VP Jerry Wexler in Nashville in 1972, leading to Nelson's signing with Atlantic for their new country division. He rewrote it for "Phases and Stages," changing the spelling to "M-A-R-Y" and the narrative to a man migrating to Texas from Los Angeles to forget a former lover. It reached number 17 on the Billboard Country Chart in 1974 and became a staple of Nelson's live shows. It was produced by R&B legend Jerry Wexler and inspired by Nelson's desire to be a better parent. "Bloody Mary Morning, that is actually from the pilot episode of Austin City Limits that was written by Willie Nelson produced by R&B Legend, Jerry Wexler and forever after that a staple of Willie's live shows."

podcast.body: This was the original title of "Bloody Mary Morning" and was included on Willie Nelson's 1970 album, "Both Sides Now." "So the original title was Bloody Mary, M-E-R-R-Y, not M-A-R-Y as it is now known."
